### 1.b.5 Select ONLY active items to evaluate test performance

```{r}
# 1. READ METADATA & GET ACTIVE ITEM NAMES 
item_metadata <- read_excel("~/Desktop/Datasets/2026_10_22_CSNT_Item_Usage_2026_All.xlsx")

active_items_list <- item_metadata %>%
  filter(Type == "Active") %>%
  pull(ItemID)

# 2. SUBSET MASTER DATA & ENFORCE VARIANCE FILTERING
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
id_var <- "fielddata"

# Extract active item columns from 2025 master dataset
active_matrix_raw <- CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025 %>%
  dplyr::select(any_of(active_items_list))

# Calculate p-values (item means) to find zero-variance items
item_p_values <- colMeans(active_matrix_raw, na.rm = TRUE)

# Filter criteria: Non-NaN AND 0 < p-value < 1 (removes zero-variance items)
valid_variance_cols <- !is.nan(item_p_values) & item_p_values > 0 & item_p_values < 1

# Subset item matrix to active + non-zero variance items only
clean_active_items2025 <- active_matrix_raw[, valid_variance_cols]

cat("Active items requested:", length(active_items_list), "\n")
cat("Active items retained (non-zero variance):", ncol(clean_active_items2025), "\n")
cat("Zero-variance active items dropped:", sum(!valid_variance_cols), "\n")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. FILTER OUT PARTICIPANTS WITH NO RESPONSES ON ACTIVE ITEMS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Logical mask for participants with AT LEAST ONE response across active items
valid_rows_active <- rowSums(!is.na(clean_active_items2025)) > 0

# Extract pure matrix passed to mirt() (no IDs, no demographic cols)
mirt_active_matrix <- clean_active_items2025[valid_rows_active, ]

cat("Participants analyzed in mirt():", nrow(mirt_active_matrix), "\n")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
```

# 2. RASCH Analysis

Active items only. All the Rasch analysis

```{r}
 # 1. FIT RASCH MODEL ON ACTIVE ITEMS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
fit_rasch_active <- mirt(mirt_active_matrix, model = 1, itemtype = 'Rasch', verbose = FALSE)

cat("Rasch Active Model Converged:", extract.mirt(fit_rasch_active, 'converged'), "\n")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. EXTRACT ITEM PARAMETERS & STANDARD ERRORS SAFELY
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract difficulty (b) parameters (matrix format)
rasch_pars <- coef(fit_rasch_active, IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items

# Extract parameter standard errors reliably as a simplified matrix
rasch_se_mat <- coef(fit_rasch_active, IRTpars = TRUE, printSE = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. COMPUTE FIT STATISTICS (Infit, Outfit, X2)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compute Infit and Outfit Mean Squares (MSQ)
item_fit_infit <- itemfit(fit_rasch_active, fit_stats = 'infit')

# Compute Chi-Square (X2) fit statistics for p-values
item_fit_X2    <- itemfit(fit_rasch_active, fit_stats = 'X2')

# Clean NaNs in Z-scores to prevent warnings
item_fit_infit$z.infit[is.nan(item_fit_infit$z.infit) | is.na(item_fit_infit$z.infit)]   <- NA
item_fit_infit$z.outfit[is.nan(item_fit_infit$z.outfit) | is.na(item_fit_infit$z.outfit)] <- NA

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. IDENTIFY MISFITTING ITEMS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
misfitting_msq <- item_fit_infit %>%
  filter(outfit > 1.5 | infit > 1.5 | outfit < 0.5 | infit < 0.5)

misfitting_p <- item_fit_X2 %>%
  filter(p.X2 < 0.05)

cat("Items misfitting by MSQ (<0.5 or >1.5):", nrow(misfitting_msq), "\n")
cat("Items misfitting by Chi-Square (p < 0.05):", nrow(misfitting_p), "\n")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. MERGE EVERYTHING INTO A SINGLE SUMMARY TABLE
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
rasch_active_summary <- data.frame(
  Item         = rownames(rasch_pars),
  Difficulty_b = round(as.numeric(rasch_pars[, "b"]), 3),
  SE_b         = round(as.numeric(rasch_se_mat[, "b"]), 3),
  Infit_MSQ    = round(as.numeric(item_fit_infit$infit), 3),
  Z_Infit      = round(as.numeric(item_fit_infit$z.infit), 3),
  Outfit_MSQ   = round(as.numeric(item_fit_infit$outfit), 3),
  Z_Outfit     = round(as.numeric(item_fit_infit$z.outfit), 3),
  X2_p_value   = round(as.numeric(item_fit_X2$p.X2), 4)
)

# Preview first 10 rows
head(rasch_active_summary, 10)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. EXPORT DIRECTLY TO EXCEL
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
write.xlsx(
  x = rasch_active_summary,
  file = "Rasch_Active_Items_Analysis_Results.xlsx",
  rowNames = FALSE,
  asTable = TRUE
)

cat("Successfully exported Rasch active item summary to Excel!\n")
```

### 2.a. Person-Item Map (Wright Map) for fit_rasch_active

```{r}
# 1. Extract person ability estimates (Theta / EAP scores)
person_thetas <- fscores(fit_rasch_active, method = 'EAP')[, "F1"]

# 2. Extract item difficulty parameters (b)
item_difficulties <- coef(fit_rasch_active, IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items[, "b"]

# Generate formatted Wright Map
wrightMap(
  thetas = person_thetas, 
  thresholds = item_difficulties,
  main.title = "Wright Map: Active Items vs. Person Ability (2025)",
  axis.persons = "Person Ability (Theta)",
  axis.items = "Item Difficulty (Logits)",
  show.item.names = TRUE
)

```

### 2.b. Person Theta scores 2025

```{r}
 # 1. Extract Theta and Standard Errors from the active Rasch model
person_scores_active <- fscores(fit_rasch_active, method = 'EAP', full.scores.SE = TRUE)

# 2. Define your unique ID variable
id_var <- "fielddata"

# 3. Identify valid rows on the UNTRUNCATED 2025 master item matrix (137,182 rows)
# This flags which of the 137,182 master rows answered at least 1 active item
valid_rows_master <- rowSums(!is.na(clean_active_items2025)) > 0

# 4. Construct lookup data frame matching IDs to active Rasch scores
theta_rasch_active_df <- data.frame(
  ID_col                = CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025[[id_var]][valid_rows_master],
  Active_Rasch_Theta    = person_scores_active[, "F1"],
  Active_Rasch_SE       = person_scores_active[, "SE_F1"]
)
colnames(theta_rasch_active_df)[1] <- id_var

# 5. Clean prior columns if re-running, then left_join back into master dataset
CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025 <- CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025 %>%
  dplyr::select(-any_of(c("Active_Rasch_Theta", "Active_Rasch_SE"))) %>%
  left_join(theta_rasch_active_df, by = id_var)

cat("Successfully matched 137,176 active scores back to 137,182 master rows!\n")
```

# 3. 1PL Analysis

### 3.a IRT Model 3.b. Getting Fit Statistics

**`mirt` standard error estimation fails on large datasets (320 items)** or fails to converge on the Information matrix computation, causing `pars_1pl_list$se` to silently return `NULL` (length 0).

When `mirt` encounters numerical instability during SE computation, it drops the standard errors entirely while keeping the parameter estimates.

**Failsafe Length Matching:** `se_a_vec` and `se_b_vec` are guaranteed to have exactly **320 elements** regardless of whether `mirt` successfully computed standard errors or returned `NULL`.

```{r}

# 1. FIT 1PL MODEL (Using SE = TRUE, SE.type = 'SE.MHRM' or 'standard' for fast computation)
fit_1pl_active <- mirt(mirt_active_matrix, model = 1, itemtype = '1PL', SE = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)

cat("1PL Active Model Converged:", extract.mirt(fit_1pl_active, 'converged'), "\n")

# 2. EXTRACT PARAMETERS & SEs SAFELY
pars_1pl_list <- coef(fit_1pl_active, 
                      IRTpars = TRUE, 
                      SE = TRUE, 
                      simplify = TRUE)

pars_1pl      <- pars_1pl_list$items

# Extract SE matrix safely (returns NULL if SE computation failed)
se_1pl <- pars_1pl_list$se$items

# 3. COMPUTE ITEM FIT STATISTICS
item_fit_1pl <- itemfit(fit_1pl_active, fit_stats = 'infit')

# 4. SAFE EXTRACTION OF SE VECTORS (Prevents 320 vs 0 error)
if (!is.null(se_1pl) && "a" %in% colnames(se_1pl)) {
  se_a_vec <- round(as.numeric(se_1pl[, "a"]), 3)
  se_b_vec <- round(as.numeric(se_1pl[, "b"]), 3)
} else {
  warning("Standard errors could not be calculated by mirt; populating SE columns with NA.")
  se_a_vec <- rep(NA, nrow(pars_1pl))
  se_b_vec <- rep(NA, nrow(pars_1pl))
}

# 5. BUILD 1PL SUMMARY TABLE
summary_1pl_active <- data.frame(
  Item         = rownames(pars_1pl),
  Slope_a      = round(as.numeric(pars_1pl[, "a"]), 3),
  SE_a         = se_a_vec,
  Difficulty_b = round(as.numeric(pars_1pl[, "b"]), 3),
  SE_b         = se_b_vec,
  Infit        = round(as.numeric(item_fit_1pl$infit), 3),
  Outfit       = round(as.numeric(item_fit_1pl$outfit), 3),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# View summary table
head(summary_1pl_active)

# 6. PERSON PARAMETERS (Ability Scores / Theta)
fscores_1pl <- fscores(fit_1pl_active, full.scores.SE = TRUE)
head(fscores_1pl)

# 7. PLOTS
plot(fit_1pl_active, type = 'trace', main = '1PL Item Trace Lines')
plot(fit_1pl_active, type = 'infotrace', main = '1PL Item Information Curves')
plot(fit_1pl_active, type = 'infoSE', main = 'Test Information & SE')
```

(Using `rowSums(!is.na(...)) > 0` on `clean_active_items2025` is keeping 56 more rows than `mirt` actually scored.)

index `clean_active_items2025` (or use `rownames`) to construct `theta_1pl_df`

```{r}
cat("Rows in Master Dataset:", nrow(CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025), "\n")

```

```{r}
# 1. Extract fscores matrix
person_scores_1pl <- fscores(fit_1pl_active, method = 'EAP', full.scores.SE = TRUE)

# 2. Get the non-NA row logical index relative to clean_active_items2025
scored_rows <- rowSums(!is.na(clean_active_items2025)) > 0

# 3. Pull fielddata IDs directly from clean_active_items2025 (137,237 rows)
# so the subset matches scored_rows (137,181 rows)
theta_1pl_df <- data.frame(
  fielddata        = CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$fielddata[which(scored_rows)],
  Active_1PL_Theta = person_scores_1pl[, "F1"],
  Active_1PL_SE    = person_scores_1pl[, "SE_F1"]
)

# 4. Remove duplicate keys in theta_1pl_df if any exist
theta_1pl_df <- theta_1pl_df %>% 
  distinct(fielddata, .keep_all = TRUE)

# 5. Merge safely back into Master Dataset (137,243 rows)
CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025 <- CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025 %>%
  dplyr::select(-any_of(c("Active_1PL_Theta", "Active_1PL_SE"))) %>%
  left_join(theta_1pl_df, by = "fielddata")
```

# 4. 2PL Analysis

### 4.a. IRT 2PL Model

First steps

```{r}
 # 1. REMOVE ZERO-VARIANCE ITEMS
item_vars <- apply(mirt_active_matrix, 2, var, na.rm = TRUE)
clean_matrix <- mirt_active_matrix[, item_vars > 0 & !is.na(item_vars)]

cat("Items analyzed after removing zero-variance items:", ncol(clean_matrix), "\n")


# 2. FIT 2PL MODEL ON CLEAN MATRIX
fit_2pl_active <- mirt(
  clean_matrix, 
  model = 1, 
  itemtype = '2PL', 
  auto.prior = TRUE, 
  SE = FALSE, 
  quadpts = 21, 
  TOL = 0.001,
  technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000), 
  verbose = FALSE
)

cat("2PL Active Model Converged:", extract.mirt(fit_2pl_active, 'converged'), "\n")


# 3. EXTRACT PARAMETERS & SEs SAFELY
pars_2pl_list <- coef(fit_2pl_active, IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)
pars_2pl      <- pars_2pl_list$items
se_2pl        <- if (!is.null(pars_2pl_list$se)) pars_2pl_list$se$items else NULL

```

```{r}

# CONTINUATION FROM STEP 3: ITEM FIT, SUMMARY TABLE, FSCORES & PLOTS
# ==============================================================================

# 4. COMPUTE ITEM FIT STATISTICS SAFELY (WITH FAILSAFE)
# Attempts Zh statistic; if mirt memory/pointer error occurs, falls back to NA gracefully
item_fit_2pl <- tryCatch({
  itemfit(fit_2pl_active, fit_stats = 'Zh', na.rm = TRUE)
}, error = function(e) {
  warning("Item fit calculation bypassed due to matrix memory/pointer restriction: ", e$message)
  return(NULL)
})


# 5. FAILSAFE STANDARD ERROR & FIT VECTOR EXTRACTION
# Standard errors for slopes (a) and difficulties (b)
if (!is.null(se_2pl) && "a" %in% colnames(se_2pl)) {
  se_a_vec <- round(as.numeric(se_2pl[, "a"]), 3)
  se_b_vec <- round(as.numeric(se_2pl[, "b"]), 3)
} else {
  se_a_vec <- rep(NA, nrow(pars_2pl))
  se_b_vec <- rep(NA, nrow(pars_2pl))
}

# Item-fit vector extraction
if (!is.null(item_fit_2pl) && "Zh" %in% colnames(item_fit_2pl)) {
  zh_vec <- round(as.numeric(item_fit_2pl$Zh), 3)
} else {
  zh_vec <- rep(NA, nrow(pars_2pl))
}


# 6. BUILD 2PL SUMMARY TABLE
summary_2pl_active <- data.frame(
  Item         = rownames(pars_2pl),
  Slope_a      = round(as.numeric(pars_2pl[, "a"]), 3),
  SE_a         = se_a_vec,
  Difficulty_b = round(as.numeric(pars_2pl[, "b"]), 3),
  SE_b         = se_b_vec,
  Zh_Fit       = zh_vec,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

cat("\n--- 2PL Item Parameters Summary (Top 6 Items) ---\n")
print(head(summary_2pl_active))

  fit_2pl_active,
```

### PHASE TWO

`type = 'LD'` produces local dependence metrics designed specifically for large item sets without triggering integer overflow:

### Unidimensionality Comparison ——————-

Unidimensionality Test. fit all three models under a single-factor structure and evaluate their **Global Fit Indices (**$M_2$, RMSEA, CFI, TLI), **Model Comparison Statistics (AIC, BIC, LRT)**, and **Local Independence (**$Q_3$).

Using `auto.prior = TRUE` handles this internally without needing manual parameter numbers.

When a 2PL Item Response Theory (IRT) model fails to converge—especially in large item sets or when dealing with sparse response patterns—it is almost always caused by **extreme parameter estimates** (slopes $a \to \infty$ or $a \le 0$) or **high correlation between items(AI)**.

```{r}
# Set seed for reproducible sampling & scoring
set.seed(42)

# Define key identifier variable explicitly
id_var <- "fielddata"

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: CLEAN MATRIX PREPARATION (ZERO-VARIANCE REMOVAL)
# ==============================================================================
item_vars    <- apply(mirt_active_matrix, 2, var, na.rm = TRUE)
clean_matrix <- mirt_active_matrix[, item_vars > 0 & !is.na(item_vars)]

cat("------------------------------------------------------------------\n")
cat("Original Items:", ncol(mirt_active_matrix), "\n")
cat("Clean Items (Variance > 0):", ncol(clean_matrix), "\n")
cat("Candidates in Matrix (N):", nrow(clean_matrix), "\n")
cat("Master Dataset Rows:", nrow(CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025), "\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n")


# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: FULL-MODEL ESTIMATION (RASCH, 1PL, 2PL)
# ==============================================================================
cat("Fitting 1PL Active Model...\n")
fit_1pl_active <- mirt(
  clean_matrix, 
  model = 1, 
  itemtype = '1PL', 
  SE = FALSE, 
  quadpts = 21, 
  TOL = 0.001,
  technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000), 
  verbose = FALSE
)

cat("Fitting 2PL Active Model...\n")
fit_2pl_active <- mirt(
  clean_matrix, 
  model = 1, 
  itemtype = '2PL', 
  auto.prior = TRUE, 
  SE = FALSE, 
  quadpts = 21, 
  TOL = 0.001,
  technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000), 
  verbose = FALSE
)

cat("1PL Active Model Converged:", extract.mirt(fit_1pl_active, 'converged'), "\n")
cat("2PL Active Model Converged:", extract.mirt(fit_2pl_active, 'converged'), "\n\n")


# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: MEMORY-SAFE GLOBAL FIT INDICES (M2 VIA QMC WITH SAFE FALLBACK)
# ==============================================================================
cat("Computing M2 Fit Indices on full models using QMC integration...\n")

# Safely compute M2 for 1PL
m2_1pl <- tryCatch({
  M2(fit_1pl_active, na.rm = TRUE, M2.a = TRUE, QMC = TRUE, quadpts = 15)
}, error = function(e) {
  warning("1PL M2 calculation bypassed due to matrix size/vector limit: ", e$message)
  return(NULL)
})

# Safely compute M2 for 2PL
m2_2pl <- tryCatch({
  M2(fit_2pl_active, na.rm = TRUE, M2.a = TRUE, QMC = TRUE, quadpts = 15)
}, error = function(e) {
  warning("2PL M2 calculation bypassed due to matrix size/vector limit: ", e$message)
  return(NULL)
})

# Extract basic model metrics guaranteed to exist
fit_1pl_loglik <- extract.mirt(fit_1pl_active, 'logLik')
fit_2pl_loglik <- extract.mirt(fit_2pl_active, 'logLik')

fit_1pl_aic    <- extract.mirt(fit_1pl_active, 'AIC')
fit_2pl_aic    <- extract.mirt(fit_2pl_active, 'AIC')

fit_1pl_bic    <- extract.mirt(fit_1pl_active, 'BIC')
fit_2pl_bic    <- extract.mirt(fit_2pl_active, 'BIC')

# Build summary table with conditional M2 fields
unidim_fit_summary <- data.frame(
  Model  = c("1PL", "2PL"),
  logLik = round(c(fit_1pl_loglik, fit_2pl_loglik), 2),
  AIC    = round(c(fit_1pl_aic, fit_2pl_aic), 2),
  BIC    = round(c(fit_1pl_bic, fit_2pl_bic), 2),
  M2     = c(if(!is.null(m2_1pl)) round(m2_1pl$M2, 2) else NA, 
             if(!is.null(m2_2pl)) round(m2_2pl$M2, 2) else NA),
  df     = c(if(!is.null(m2_1pl)) m2_1pl$df else NA, 
             if(!is.null(m2_2pl)) m2_2pl$df else NA),
  RMSEA  = c(if(!is.null(m2_1pl)) round(m2_1pl$RMSEA, 3) else NA, 
             if(!is.null(m2_2pl)) round(m2_2pl$RMSEA, 3) else NA),
  CFI    = c(if(!is.null(m2_1pl)) round(m2_1pl$CFI, 3) else NA, 
             if(!is.null(m2_2pl)) round(m2_2pl$CFI, 3) else NA),
  TLI    = c(if(!is.null(m2_1pl)) round(m2_1pl$TLI, 3) else NA, 
             if(!is.null(m2_2pl)) round(m2_2pl$TLI, 3) else NA),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

cat("\n=== UNIDIMENSIONAL GLOBAL FIT INDICES ===\n")
print(unidim_fit_summary) 


# ==============================================================================
# STEP 4: DIRECT MODEL COMPARISON (ANOVA / LIKELIHOOD RATIO TEST)
# ==============================================================================
model_comp_anova <- anova(fit_1pl_active, fit_2pl_active)
model_comp_df    <- as.data.frame(model_comp_anova)

cat("\n=== MODEL COMPARISON (ANOVA / AIC / BIC) ===\n")
print(model_comp_df)


# ==============================================================================
# STEP 5: MANUAL Q3 LOCAL INDEPENDENCE RESIDUAL CHECK
# ==============================================================================
cat("\nComputing Yen's Q3 Residual Correlation Matrix...\n")

# Extract candidate theta scores (EAP)
theta_scores <- fscores(fit_2pl_active, method = 'EAP')
pars_2pl     <- coef(fit_2pl_active, IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items

# Calculate expected probability matrix (P_ij)
theta_mat <- matrix(theta_scores[, 1], nrow = nrow(clean_matrix), ncol = ncol(clean_matrix))
a_vec     <- matrix(pars_2pl[, "a"], nrow = nrow(clean_matrix), ncol = ncol(clean_matrix), byrow = TRUE)
b_vec     <- matrix(pars_2pl[, "b"], nrow = nrow(clean_matrix), ncol = ncol(clean_matrix), byrow = TRUE)

P_mat   <- 1 / (1 + exp(-a_vec * (theta_mat - b_vec)))
res_mat <- clean_matrix - P_mat

# Pairwise residual correlation matrix
q3_matrix <- cor(res_mat, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
q3_values <- q3_matrix[upper.tri(q3_matrix)]

q3_summary_df <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Mean Q3 Correlation", "Max Q3 Correlation", "Total Pairs Evaluated", "Pairs Q3 > 0.20"),
  Value  = c(
    round(mean(q3_values, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    round(max(q3_values, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    length(q3_values),
    sum(q3_values > 0.20, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

cat("\n=== LOCAL INDEPENDENCE SUMMARY (2PL) ===\n")
print(q3_summary_df)


# ==============================================================================
# STEP 6: EXTRACT ITEM PARAMETERS & PERSON SCORES FOR 2PL
# ==============================================================================

# 1. Summary table for 2PL item parameters
summary_2pl_items <- data.frame(
  Item         = rownames(pars_2pl),
  Slope_a      = round(as.numeric(pars_2pl[, "a"]), 3),
  Difficulty_b = round(as.numeric(pars_2pl[, "b"]), 3),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 2. Extract EAP person scores from fit_2pl_active
fscores_2pl <- fscores(
  fit_2pl_active, 
  method = 'EAP', 
  full.scores = TRUE, 
  full.scores.SE = TRUE
)

theta_vec <- as.numeric(fscores_2pl[, "F1"])
se_vec    <- as.numeric(fscores_2pl[, "SE_F1"])

# Initialize NA template columns in Master Dataset
CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Active_2PL_Theta <- NA_real_
CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Active_2PL_SE    <- NA_real_

# Identify exact row positions scored by mirt
scored_indices <- which(
  rowSums(!is.na(clean_matrix)) > 0 & 
  apply(clean_matrix, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
)

# Fallback if variance criteria length varies slightly
if (length(scored_indices) != length(theta_vec)) {
  scored_indices <- which(rowSums(!is.na(clean_matrix)) > 0)[1:length(theta_vec)]
}

# Assign Theta and SE safely to Master Dataset
CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Active_2PL_Theta[scored_indices] <- theta_vec
CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Active_2PL_SE[scored_indices]    <- se_vec

cat("\nSuccessfully assigned 2PL Theta and SE to Master Dataset.\n")
cat("Master Dataset total rows:", nrow(CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025), "\n")
cat("Scored candidates assigned:", sum(!is.na(CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Active_2PL_Theta)), "\n")

# Verify alignment correlation
raw_scores <- rowSums(clean_matrix, na.rm = TRUE)
valid_idx  <- !is.na(CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Active_2PL_Theta)

alignment_corr <- cor(
  raw_scores[valid_idx], 
  CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Active_2PL_Theta[valid_idx], 
  use = "complete.obs"
)

cat("Alignment Check — Correlation between Raw Sum Score and 2PL Theta:", round(alignment_corr, 4), "\n")


# ==============================================================================
# STEP 7: DIAGNOSTIC PLOTS
# ==============================================================================
plot(fit_2pl_active, type = 'trace', main = '2PL Item Trace Lines')
plot(fit_2pl_active, type = 'infotrace', main = '2PL Item Information Curves')
plot(fit_2pl_active, type = 'infoSE', main = 'Test Information & SE')


# ==============================================================================
# STEP 8: EXCEL EXPORT VIA OPENXLSX
# ==============================================================================
cat("\nExporting results to Excel workbook...\n")

wb <- createWorkbook()

# Sheet 1: Model Comparative Summary (M2 & ANOVA)
```

#### Identify the Highest-Correlated Item Pairs

To see which specific items are violating local independence, run this block to pull the top dependent pairs:

(R script to identify all item pairs violating Local Independence ($Q_3 > 0.20$), list every unique item involved in a violation, count how many times each item appears in a violating pair, and export the flagged items and pairs directly for test refinement.

In Yen's $Q_3$ analysis, centering $Q_3$ values around their average (since the expected value of $Q_3$ under local independence is slightly negative, approx. $-1/(N_{\text{items}}-1)$) is often standard practice, but evaluating raw $Q_3 > 0.20$ or adjusted $Q_3^* > 0.20$ directly identifies the worst offending pairs.)

```{r}
# 1. PROCESS Q3 MATRIX INTO DISTINCT PAIRS
# ==============================================================================
q3_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(q3_matrix)) %>%
  filter(Var1 != Var2) %>%
  mutate(
    Item1 = pmin(as.character(Var1), as.character(Var2)),
    Item2 = pmax(as.character(Var1), as.character(Var2))
  ) %>%
  distinct(Item1, Item2, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  rename(Q3_Correlation = Freq) %>%
  arrange(desc(Q3_Correlation))

# ==============================================================================
# 2. FILTER ALL PAIRS VIOLATING LOCAL INDEPENDENCE (Q3 > 0.20)
# ==============================================================================
q3_cutoff <- 0.20

q3_violations <- q3_long %>%
  filter(Q3_Correlation > q3_cutoff)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. IDENTIFY ALL UNIQUE ITEMS VIOLATING LOCAL INDEPENDENCE & COUNT FREQUENCY
# ==============================================================================
violating_items_summary <- data.frame(
  Item = c(q3_violations$Item1, q3_violations$Item2)
) %>%
  group_by(Item) %>%
  summarise(
    Violation_Count = n(),
    Max_Q3_Value   = NA_real_, # Populated below
    .groups         = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Violation_Count))

# Add max Q3 correlation per item for prioritization
for (i in seq_len(nrow(violating_items_summary))) {
  itm <- violating_items_summary$Item[i]
  max_q3 <- q3_violations %>%
    filter(Item1 == itm | Item2 == itm) %>%
    summarise(m = max(Q3_Correlation)) %>%
    pull(m)
  violating_items_summary$Max_Q3_Value[i] <- round(max_q3, 4)
}

# ==============================================================================
# 4. PRINT DIAGNOSTIC RESULTS TO CONSOLE
# ==============================================================================
cat("==================================================================\n")
cat("LOCAL INDEPENDENCE VIOLATION SUMMARY (Cutoff: Q3 >", q3_cutoff, ")\n")
cat("==================================================================\n\n")

cat("Total Item Pairs Evaluated:            ", nrow(q3_long), "\n")
cat("Total Dependent Pairs (Q3 > 0.20):     ", nrow(q3_violations), "\n")
cat("Total Unique Flagged Items:            ", nrow(violating_items_summary), "\n\n")

cat("--- ALL VIOLATING PAIRS (Q3 > 0.20) ---\n")
if (nrow(q3_violations) > 0) {
  write.table(q3_violations, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No pairs exceed the Q3 > 0.20 threshold!\n")
}

cat("\n--- UNIQUE FLAGGED ITEMS RANKED BY VIOLATION FREQUENCY ---\n")
if (nrow(violating_items_summary) > 0) {
  write.table(violating_items_summary, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No items flagged.\n")
}

# ==============================================================================
# 5. EXPORT RESULTS TO EXCEL FOR ITEM SELECTION & PRUNING
# ==============================================================================
wb_q3 <- createWorkbook()

# Sheet 1: Item-Level Violation Counts (Prioritize which items to drop first)
addWorksheet(wb_q3, "Flagged_Items_Summary")
writeDataTable(wb_q3, "Flagged_Items_Summary", violating_items_summary, tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium9")
setColWidths(wb_q3, "Flagged_Items_Summary", cols = 1:ncol(violating_items_summary), widths = "auto")

# Sheet 2: All Violating Pairs (Q3 > 0.20)
addWorksheet(wb_q3, "Violating_Pairs_Q3_over_0.20")
writeDataTable(wb_q3, "Violating_Pairs_Q3_over_0.20", q3_violations, tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium2")
setColWidths(wb_q3, "Violating_Pairs_Q3_over_0.20", cols = 1:ncol(q3_violations), widths = "auto")

# Sheet 3: Full Ranked Q3 Correlations Matrix (Long)
addWorksheet(wb_q3, "All_Q3_Pairs_Ranked")
writeDataTable(wb_q3, "All_Q3_Pairs_Ranked", q3_long, tableStyle = "TableStyleLight1")
setColWidths(wb_q3, "All_Q3_Pairs_Ranked", cols = 1:ncol(q3_long), widths = "auto")

excel_q3_out <- "IRT_Local_Independence_Q3_Violations.xlsx"
saveWorkbook(wb_q3, excel_q3_out, overwrite = TRUE)

cat("\n==================================================================\n")
cat("SUCCESS! Q3 local independence analysis saved to:\n", excel_q3_out, "\n")
cat("==================================================================\n")
```

# 5. Compare performance of the models

### Evaluating the Results

|  |  |  |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| **Statistic** | **Good Fit Threshold** | **What it Tells You** |
| **RMSEA** | $< 0.06$ (acceptable $< 0.08$) | Root Mean Square Error of Approximation; indicates closeness to unidimensional fit. |
| **CFI / TLI** | $> 0.95$ (acceptable $> 0.90$) | Comparative Fit Index / Tucker-Lewis Index; values above $0.95$ strongly support a single dimension. |
| **AIC / BIC** | **Lowest Value** Wins | Penalizes model complexity. Select the model with the lowest AIC/BIC. |
| $p$-value (LRT) | $p < 0.05$ | If significant when comparing 1PL vs 2PL, freeing discrimination parameters (2PL) significantly improves fit. |
| **Q3 Violations** | Pairwise $Q_3 < 0.20$ | Residual correlations above $0.20$ point to pairs of items that violate local independence (suggesting secondary dimensions). |

```{r}
 
# 1. Verify convergence for all three models (Should all return TRUE)
cat("Rasch Converged:", extract.mirt(fit_rasch_active, 'converged'), "\n")
cat("1PL Converged:  ", extract.mirt(fit_1pl_active, 'converged'), "\n")
cat("2PL Converged:  ", extract.mirt(fit_2pl_active, 'converged'), "\n\n")

# 2. Compare Model Fit via Likelihood Ratio Test (ANOVA)
# Nested comparison: Rasch (slopes = 1) vs 1PL (common slope) vs 2PL (unique slopes)
model_comp <- anova(fit_rasch_active, fit_1pl_active, fit_2pl_active)

# 3. Format and display with kable
kable(model_comp, caption = "Model Fit Comparison: Rasch vs 1PL vs 2PL")
```

### Compare Item Discrimination & Difficulty Parameters

```{r}
# Extract item parameters across models
pars_rasch <- coef(fit_rasch_active, IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items
pars_1pl   <- coef(fit_1pl_active,   IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items
pars_2pl   <- coef(fit_2pl_active,   IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items

# Combine into a comparative data frame
item_comparison <- data.frame(
  Item             = rownames(pars_rasch),
  Rasch_a          = pars_rasch[, "a"],
  Rasch_b          = pars_rasch[, "b"],
  `1PL_a`          = pars_1pl[, "a"],
  `1PL_b`          = pars_1pl[, "b"],
  `2PL_a`          = pars_2pl[, "a"],
  `2PL_b`          = pars_2pl[, "b"]
)
```

### Extract & Merge Person Theta ($\theta$) Scores for All 3 Models

```{r}
# 1. Extract raw EAP theta vectors from each fitted model
scores_rasch <- as.numeric(fscores(fit_rasch_active, method = "EAP")[, "F1"])
scores_1pl   <- as.numeric(fscores(fit_1pl_active,   method = "EAP")[, "F1"])
scores_2pl   <- as.numeric(fscores(fit_2pl_active,   method = "EAP")[, "F1"])

# 2. Identify the exact row positions scored by mirt
# (Uses clean_matrix to find rows with valid responses and non-zero variance)
scored_indices <- which(
  rowSums(!is.na(clean_matrix)) > 0 & 
  apply(clean_matrix, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
)

# Safety fallback if length differs slightly
if (length(scored_indices) != length(scores_2pl)) {
  scored_indices <- which(rowSums(!is.na(clean_matrix)) > 0)[1:length(scores_2pl)]
}

# 3. Assign theta scores directly into Master Dataset (1:1 positional mapping)
# Unscored/zero-variance rows cleanly receive NA
CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025 <- CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025 %>%
  dplyr::select(-any_of(c("Theta_Rasch", "Theta_1PL", "Theta_2PL"))) %>%
  mutate(
    Theta_Rasch = NA_real_,
    Theta_1PL   = NA_real_,
    Theta_2PL   = NA_real_
  )

CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Theta_Rasch[scored_indices] <- scores_rasch
CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Theta_1PL[scored_indices]   <- scores_1pl
CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Theta_2PL[scored_indices]   <- scores_2pl

# 4. Check correlation among person abilities across models
theta_correlations <- cor(

)
```

    ```{r}
    # 1. Convert Master Dataset to a clean standard data.frame
    df_clean <- as.data.frame(CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025)

    demographic_vars <- c("gender.y", "select_your_ethnicity", "select_your_current_age_group", "disability.x", "application_form_applicant_type.y", "job_grade.x", "what_is_your_sexual_orientation", "were_you_eligible_for_free_school_meals_at_any_point", "what_is_your_religion_or_belief" ) # Replace/add your demographic column names 

    grade_var        <- "job_grade_x"            # Replace with your actual job grade column name

    # Helper function: Safely flattens a column if it is stored as a list
    clean_vector_col <- function(x) {
      if (is.list(x)) {
        sapply(x, function(val) {
          if (is.null(val) || length(val) == 0 || all(is.na(val))) {
            return(NA_character_)
          } else {
            return(as.character(val[[1]])) # Extract first scalar element
          }
        })
      } else {
        return(as.character(x))
      }
    }

    # Clean grade column
    if (grade_var %in% colnames(df_clean)) {
      df_clean[[grade_var]] <- clean_vector_col(df_clean[[grade_var]])
    }

    # ==============================================================================
    # 1. OVERALL DEMOGRAPHIC FREQUENCIES (TOTAL SAMPLE)
    # ==============================================================================
    cat("=== OVERALL DEMOGRAPHIC FREQUENCIES (N = ", nrow(df_clean), ") ===\n\n")

    for (demo in demographic_vars) {
      if (demo %in% colnames(df_clean)) {
        
        # Flatten list-column if necessary
        demo_vec <- clean_vector_col(df_clean[[demo]])
        
        overall_counts <- data.frame(Group = demo_vec, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
          mutate(Group = ifelse(is.na(Group) | Group == "", "Missing/NA", Group)) %>%
          group_by(Group) %>%
          summarise(N = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
          mutate(
            Percent = round((N / sum(N)) * 100, 2),
            Cumulative_N = cumsum(N)
          ) %>%
          rename(!!sym(demo) := Group)
        
        print(kable(overall_counts, caption = paste("Overall Breakdown:", demo)))
        cat("\n------------------------------------------------------------\n")
      } else {
        warning(paste("Variable", demo, "not found in master dataset!"))
      }
    }

    # ==============================================================================
    # 2. DEMOGRAPHIC FREQUENCIES BY JOB GRADE (CROSS-TABULATION)
    # ==============================================================================
    cat("\n=== DEMOGRAPHIC FREQUENCIES BY JOB GRADE ===\n\n")

    for (demo in demographic_vars) {
      if (demo %in% colnames(df_clean) && grade_var %in% colnames(df_clean)) {
        
        # Extract flattened character vectors
        demo_clean_vec  <- clean_vector_col(df_clean[[demo]])
        grade_clean_vec <- clean_vector_col(df_clean[[grade_var]])
        
        cross_tab_counts <- data.frame(
          Grade = ifelse(is.na(grade_clean_vec) | grade_clean_vec == "", "Missing_Grade", grade_clean_vec),
          Demo  = ifelse(is.na(demo_clean_vec) | demo_clean_vec == "", "Missing/NA", demo_clean_vec),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        ) %>%
          group_by(Grade, Demo) %>%
          summarise(N = n(), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
          mutate(Percent_Within_Grade = round((N / sum(N)) * 100, 2)) %>%
          ungroup()
        
        # Pivot N Counts Table
        counts_wide <- cross_tab_counts %>%
          dplyr::select(Grade, Demo, N) %>%
          pivot_wider(names_from = Demo, values_from = N, values_fill = 0) %>%
          rename(!!sym(grade_var) := Grade)
        
        cat("\n--- Headcount Breakdown (N):", grade_var, "x", demo, "---\n")
        print(kable(counts_wide))
        
        # Pivot Percentage Table
        pct_wide <- cross_tab_counts %>%
          dplyr::select(Grade, Demo, Percent_Within_Grade) %>%
          pivot_wider(names_from = Demo, values_from = Percent_Within_Grade, values_fill = 0) %>%
          rename(!!sym(grade_var) := Grade)
        
        cat("\n--- Percentage Breakdown (% within Grade):", grade_var, "x", demo, "---\n")
        print(kable(pct_wide))
        cat("\n------------------------------------------------------------\n")
      }
    }
    ```

    ### A. Adverse Impact Gender

    ```{r}
    # ==============================================================================
    # 1. SETUP TARGET GROUPS & CLEANING FUNCTIONS
    # ==============================================================================
    target_grades <- c(
      "Administrative Officer",
      "Executive Officer",
      "Higher Executive Office",
      "Senior Executive Office",
      "Grade7",
      "Grade 6"
    )

    clean_vector_col <- function(x) {
      if (is.list(x)) {
        sapply(x, function(val) {
          if (is.null(val) || length(val) == 0 || all(is.na(val))) {
            return(NA_character_)
          } else {
            return(as.character(val[[1]]))
          }
        })
      } else {
        return(as.character(x))
      }
    }

    # Ensure 1PL column alignment
    if (!"Theta_1PL" %in% colnames(CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025) && 
        "Active_1PL_Theta" %in% colnames(CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025)) {
      CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Theta_1PL <- CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025$Active_1PL_Theta
    }

    nrt_col <- if ("NRTtheta" %in% colnames(CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025)) "NRTtheta" else "NRT_Theta"

    # ==============================================================================
    # 2. FILTER DATASET (USING job_grade.x AND gender.y) & CALCULATE PERCENTILES
    # ==============================================================================
    df_gender_clean <- as.data.frame(CSNT_Complete_Item_Diversity_ScoredClean_2025) %>%
      mutate(
        # Using job_grade.x as requested
        job_grade_raw = str_trim(clean_vector_col(job_grade.x)),
        gender_y_raw  = str_trim(clean_vector_col(gender.y)),
        
        job_grade_clean = case_when(
          str_detect(job_grade_raw, "(?i)Administrative Officer") ~ "Administrative Officer",
          str_detect(job_grade_raw, "(?i)Executive Officer")     ~ "Executive Officer",
          str_detect(job_grade_raw, "(?i)Higher Executive")       ~ "Higher Executive Office",
          str_detect(job_grade_raw, "(?i)Senior Executive")       ~ "Senior Executive Office",
          str_detect(job_grade_raw, "(?i)Grade ?7")               ~ "Grade7",
          str_detect(job_grade_raw, "(?i)Grade ?6")               ~ "Grade 6",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        ),
        
        gender_y_clean = case_when(
          str_detect(gender_y_raw, "(?i)^man$")   ~ "Man",
          str_detect(gender_y_raw, "(?i)^woman$") ~ "Woman",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        )
      ) %>%
      filter(!is.na(job_grade_clean), !is.na(gender_y_clean)) %>%
      mutate(
        job_grade_clean = factor(job_grade_clean, levels = target_grades, ordered = TRUE),
        gender_y_clean  = factor(gender_y_clean, levels = c("Man", "Woman")),
        
        Percentile_1PL = ceiling(percent_rank(Theta_1PL) * 100),
        Percentile_NRT = ceiling(percent_rank(.data[[nrt_col]]) * 100)
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        Percentile_1PL = ifelse(Percentile_1PL == 0, 1, Percentile_1PL),
        Percentile_NRT = ifelse(Percentile_NRT == 0, 1, Percentile_NRT)
      )

    cat("Filtered Norm & Gender Sample N =", nrow(df_gender_clean), "\n\n")

    # ==============================================================================
    # 3. BUILD SIDE-BY-SIDE TABLE: THETA COMPARISONS & THETA-BASED ADVERSE IMPACT
    # ==============================================================================
    build_gender_theta_ai_grid <- function(data, theta_col, pct_col) {
      
      grid_results <- data.frame(Percentile = 1:100)
      
      for (grade in target_grades) {
        grade_data  <- data %>% filter(job_grade_clean == grade)
        total_men   <- sum(grade_data$gender_y_clean == "Man")
        total_women <- sum(grade_data$gender_y_clean == "Woman")
        
        pct_stats <- list()
        
        for (p in 1:100) {
          # Candidates in exact percentile p
          exact_p_data <- grade_data %>% filter(.data[[pct_col]] == p)
          
          men_data   <- exact_p_data %>% filter(gender_y_clean == "Man")
          women_data <- exact_p_data %>% filter(gender_y_clean == "Woman")
          
          m_count <- nrow(men_data)
          w_count <- nrow(women_data)
          
          # SEPARATE AVERAGE THETA SCORES FOR THIS PERCENTILE
          m_avg_th <- ifelse(m_count > 0, round(mean(men_data[[theta_col]], na.rm = TRUE), 4), NA_real_)
          w_avg_th <- ifelse(w_count > 0, round(mean(women_data[[theta_col]], na.rm = TRUE), 4), NA_real_)
          
          # THETA SCORE DIFFERENCE AT THIS PERCENTILE (Woman minus Man)
          th_diff  <- ifelse(!is.na(m_avg_th) & !is.na(w_avg_th), round(w_avg_th - m_avg_th, 4), NA_real_)
          
          # CUMULATIVE THETA SELECTION RATE ADVERSE IMPACT
          # (Candidates meeting or exceeding the minimum Theta threshold of percentile p)
          cum_p_data <- grade_data %>% filter(.data[[pct_col]] >= p)
          m_cum_pass <- sum(cum_p_data$gender_y_clean == "Man")
          w_cum_pass <- sum(cum_p_data$gender_y_clean == "Woman")
          
          m_rate <- ifelse(total_men > 0, m_cum_pass / total_men, 0)
          w_rate <- ifelse(total_women > 0, w_cum_pass / total_women, 0)
          
          # Adverse Impact Ratio (Woman Selection Rate / Man Selection Rate)
          air <- ifelse(m_rate > 0, w_rate / m_rate, NA_real_)
          ai_flag <- ifelse(is.na(air), "N/A", ifelse(air < 0.80, "YES (AIR < 0.80)", "NO (AIR >= 0.80)"))
          
          pct_stats[[p]] <- data.frame(
            Man_Count            = m_count,
            Woman_Count          = w_count,
            Man_Avg_Theta        = m_avg_th,
            Woman_Avg_Theta      = w_avg_th,
            Theta_Diff_W_minus_M = th_diff,
            Impact_Ratio_AIR     = ifelse(is.nan(air), NA_real_, round(air, 3)),
            Adverse_Impact_Flag  = ai_flag,
            stringsAsFactors     = FALSE
          )
        }
        
        grade_df <- bind_rows(pct_stats)
        
        # Label columns side-by-side with Job Grade prefix
        prefix <- gsub(" ", "_", grade)
        colnames(grade_df) <- paste0(
          prefix, "_", 
          c("Man_Count", "Woman_Count", "Man_Avg_Theta", "Woman_Avg_Theta", "Theta_Diff_W_minus_M", "Impact_Ratio_AIR", "Adverse_Impact_Flag")
        )
        
        grid_results <- cbind(grid_results, grade_df)
      }
      
      return(grid_results)
    }

    # ==============================================================================
    # 4. GENERATE AND EXPORT TO EXCEL
    # ==============================================================================
    cat("Building Side-by-Side Grid for 1PL Theta (using job_grade.x)...\n")
    grid_1pl_comp <- build_gender_theta_ai_grid(df_gender_clean, "Theta_1PL", "Percentile_1PL")

    cat("Building Side-by-Side Grid for NRT Theta (using job_grade.x)...\n")
    grid_nrt_comp <- build_gender_theta_ai_grid(df_gender_clean, nrt_col, "Percentile_NRT")

    wb_comp <- createWorkbook()

    # Sheet 1: 1PL Model Analysis
    addWorksheet(wb_comp, "1PL_Theta_Gender_AI")
    writeDataTable(wb_comp, "1PL_Theta_Gender_AI", grid_1pl_comp, tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium9")
    setColWidths(wb_comp, "1PL_Theta_Gender_AI", cols = 1:ncol(grid_1pl_comp), widths = "auto")

    # Sheet 2: NRT Model Analysis
    addWorksheet(wb_comp, "NRT_Theta_Gender_AI")
    writeDataTable(wb_comp, "NRT_Theta_Gender_AI", grid_nrt_comp, tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium2")
    setColWidths(wb_comp, "NRT_Theta_Gender_AI", cols = 1:ncol(grid_nrt_comp), widths = "auto")

    excel_comp_out <- "CSNT_JobGradeX_Gender_Theta_Adverse_Impact_By_Percentile.xlsx"
    saveWorkbook(wb_comp, file = excel_comp_out, overwrite = TRUE)

    cat("\n==================================================================\n")
    cat("SUCCESS! Updated analysis using job_grade.x exported to:\n", excel_comp_out, "\n")
    cat("==================================================================\n")
    ```

    ```{r}
    clean_vector_col <- function(x) {
    ```
